title: Visualizing Adhesion Formation in Cells by Means of Advanced Spinning Disk-Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence Microscopy
protocol: Seed 3*105 HeLa or NIH3T3 cells in 2 mL of full growth medium per well of a 6-well cell-culture plate two days prior to the experiment.
Handle cells in a laminar flow hood throughout the protocol.
Dilute 1 µg of RFP-Lifeact and 1 µg of YFP-Vinculin in a total of 200 µL reduced serum medium one day prior to the experiment.
Vortex the transfection reagent briefly, add 4 µL to 200 µL DNA, and vortex again.
Incubate the transfection mix for 15-20 min at room temperature.
Add the entire transfection mix dropwise directly to the cells.
Mix by shaking the plate and place it back into the incubator.
Prepare a 10 µg/mL solution of fibronectin in PBS to coat the glass surface of a 35 mm glass bottom dish on the day of the experiment.
Use only high quality 0.17 mm glass coverslips for optimal TIRF performance and avoid plastic bottom dishes.
Leave the fibronectin solution on the glass surface for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove the fibronectin solution and let the dish air-dry.
Dilute a 0.1 µm multi-fluorescent beads solution to a density of 1.8 x 109 particles per mL in distilled water.
Add the bead solution to the fibronectin-coated glass surface for 30-60 s.
Immediately remove the bead solution and let the dish air-dry.
Prepare a 0.1 M ascorbic acid (AA) solution.
Dilute the AA solution to a final concentration of 0.1 mM in growth medium (AA-medium).
Place the AA-medium solution in a 37 °C water bath.
Wash the cells with 2 mL PBS.
Add 250 µL Trypsin-EDTA and wait until the cells are fully detached (2-3 min in a 37 °C incubator).
Resuspend the detached cells carefully in 1 mL pre-warmed AA-medium using a pipette.
Transfer the resuspended cell suspension to 4 mL AA-medium in a 15 mL cell culture tube.
Place the cell suspension with a slightly opened lid in an incubator set to 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Add 1 mL pre-warmed AA-medium to the glass bottom dish.
Place the glass bottom dish in the holder of the pre-heated microscope.
Set the time-interval to 30 seconds and the duration to 60-90 minutes.
Activate the auto-focusing function of the hardware-based auto-focus for every time point.
Adjust the camera exposure and gain, as well as the laser power for every channel.
Set high gain levels, low exposure time, and low laser power to reduce photo-toxicity.
Configure the z-stack for spinning-disk channels to 10 µm with 0.4 µm spacing.
De-activate z-stacks for TIRF channels.
Set the bottom-offset to “0” for the focus position of the hardware auto-focus.
Activate the multi-point function “stage positions”.
Find the fluorescent beads with epi-fluorescent illumination at the ocular or on the computer screen.
Activate one TIRF channel and set the illumination angle to a value that denotes TIRF illumination.
Activate the auto-focus by pushing the button at the microscope panel.
Adjust the focus with the offset wheel.
Acquire a 2-color dataset, i.e., TIRF-488 and TIRF-561, for subsequent bead-based image registration.
Add a few microliters of freely floating fluorescent multicolor beads suspension to ensure TIRF illumination.
Activate the live view of a TIRF channel and increase the illumination angle.
Mix the cell suspension again by inverting the closed tube 2-3 times.
Apply 1 mL of the cells to the imaging dish.
Quickly find double-transfected cells with low level epi-fluorescent illumination.
Center the cells in the live camera preview using bright field illumination and mark the position.
Find another 1-2 points of interest and save them to the positions list.
Set 4-5 positions and re-check all before starting image acquisition.
Discard 1-2 positions.
Start data acquisition by clicking on the “Sequence” button.
Save the "SD-TIRF_helper_JoVE.ijm" macro in the FIJI sub-folder “macros”.
Run the macro via “Plugins>Macros>Run…” menu command.
Select the registration correction option if needed for color channels.
Create a new bead-based registration reference or use an existing one.
Install the turboreg plugin according to general guidelines.
Import data using the bio-formats importer and choose hyperstack viewing option.
Load image dataset, select SD-series in the first step.
Select TIRF-series in the second step after loading the dataset.
FIJI will display the sorted data by channel and stage position as hyperstacks.
Apply registration correction to respective channels by loading pre-determined landmarks file.
Select a color look-up table (LUT) for every SD- and TIRF channel.
Merge all selected LUTs into a single multi-dimensional hyperstack.
Add z-planes with zero intensity values on top of the bottom plane in the TIRF dataset to match the number of z-planes in the SD dataset.
